column2: A Japanese soroban or Chinese suanpan: beads flicked by an unseen fingertip, the time literally counted on the rods, wood, brass, click and rhythm.
Othello / Reversi: black and white discs on a green board flipping in cascades; the time is the pattern of colours, and every move flips it.
A frozen rink from above at night: figure skaters carve the time into the ice with their blades, spins and jumps; a Zamboni resurfaces it.
The Chinese incense seal clock (香篆): a slow ember burns along a maze of incense powder pressed into ash, smoke curling up; burnt and unburnt powder tell the time.
Su Song's 11th-century astronomical clock tower: a water wheel, escapement, armillary sphere, and little puppet figures appearing at doors with bells, drums and placards.
A Ouija board in candlelight: the planchette glides on its own, spelling out the time letter by letter; spirits are impatient.
A tarot reader's table: cards dealt, turned and laid in a spread; the arcana, suits and numbers on the cards are the time.
A Magic 8-Ball: dark blue liquid, the floating die rises to the window bubbling, its faces carry the answer. Shake it and ask again.
A hospital bedside monitor: ECG, pleth and respiration traces sweeping, numbers in green and cyan; the heartbeat writes the time.
A Zen dry rock garden (karesansui): raked gravel ripples around stones; a monk's rake rewrites the patterns, shadows of maple leaves drift over.
Stop-motion plasticine at 12 fps: thumbprints, boiling, squash, everything sculpted and re-sculpted by hand frame by frame (Aardman, Gumby).
A marionette theatre: puppets on visible strings and wooden control bars, a puppeteer's hands above; the strings and puppets carry the time.
The view from a night train window: lights, stations, level crossings and towns rushing past, your reflection in the glass; the time is out there in the passing world.
A beach at night where bioluminescent plankton glow electric blue as waves break and feet step; the light writes the time.
A thermal receipt printer: paper chatters out of the slot, prints the time like a till slip (items, totals, barcode), is torn off, curls and falls.
Magnetic poetry and alphabet magnets on a fridge door: a hand rearranges words and letters to say the time; postcards, notes, a child's drawing.
International maritime signal flags and numeral pennants hoisted on a ship's halyards at sea: wind, waves, sailors running them up.
Analytic cubism (Picasso, Braque): the time seen from several viewpoints at once, faceted, overlapping planes in ochre, grey and umber, slowly reassembling.
1980s Memphis Group design (Sottsass): squiggles, terrazzo, confetti, primary pastels, black-and-white patterns, bold geometric objects arranged into the time.
A lighthouse on a stormy coast at night: the lamp's beam sweeps through rain, the light characteristic flashes a code, ships answer; the time is in the light.
LEGO bricks on a baseplate seen from above: studs, bright plastic, a builder's hand snapping bricks on and off; or minifigures building it.
A wall of CCTV security monitors: grainy black-and-white feeds of corridors, car parks and lobbies, timestamps burned into the video, people crossing between cameras.
A Ferris wheel at a night funfair: gondolas turning, bulbs chasing, a midway of stalls below; the wheel, its lights or its riders tell the time.
A turntable from above: a record spinning, light catching the grooves, the tonearm tracking, a printed label; the time is in the music or on the disc.
